public_payload.normalized_proposition: The companies competing to build AI will all wind up overpaying compared to the modest profits they will be able to make in an intensely competitive regime.

statement.excerpt: Which means everybody will wind up overpaying compared to the modest profits they will be able to make in an intensely competitive regime.
statement.document_title: Why things will eventually fall apart

our_interpretation: Everybody refers to the competing AI developers discussed in the passage, including integrated firms such as Google.
Overpaying means that eventual attributable economic returns fail to justify the costs of the AI investment, including the cost of capital.
The claim concerns completed investment economics, rather than whether one quarter is profitable.
The speaker supplies no accounting basis, currency, investment cohort, profit threshold or terminal date.
Intense competition is treated as an antecedent. A provider's regulatory disclosure can establish that it faces such competition, but cannot establish that the condition will persist indefinitely.
Company-wide profits, revenue run rates and financing proceeds cannot substitute for returns attributable to AI investment.
criteria.support_condition: Under the competitive condition, completed and consistently measured investment histories show that every relevant developer earned insufficient attributable returns to justify its AI investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Under the competitive condition, at least one relevant developer conclusively earns sufficient attributable lifetime returns to justify the relevant AI investment after all associated costs and capital charges.
